definitions.explanation: Describes something of great value or importance, whether material or abstract. Often used for things that are irreplaceable or hard to obtain — time, experiences, resources, or cultural artifacts.

examples.japanese: {貴重|きちょう}な{体験|たいけん}だった。
この{美術館|びじゅつかん}には{貴重|きちょう}な{絵画|かいが}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: This art museum has many precious paintings.

examples.japanese: {限|かぎ}られた{貴重|きちょう}な{時間|じかん}を{無駄|むだ}にしたくない。
examples.english: I don't want to waste what little precious time we have.

notes:
USAGE:
A versatile adjective used across formal and informal registers. Very commonly applied to abstract concepts like {時間|じかん} (time), {経験|けいけん} (experience), and {意見|いけん} (opinion), as well as tangible items like {資料|しりょう} (documents) and {品|しな} (items).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {貴重|きちょう}な{体験|たいけん} (valuable experience)
- {貴重|きちょう}な{時間|じかん} (precious time)
- {貴重|きちょう}な{資料|しりょう} (valuable documents/materials)
- {貴重|きちょう}{品|ひん} (valuables)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {大切|たいせつ}な: important, cherished — emphasizes personal care and emotional attachment
- {希少|きしょう}な: rare, scarce — focuses specifically on rarity rather than value
